title: Spreading a supplied finite geometric closed generic cover
statement: Let f:X\to S be finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with S irreducible and generic point eta. Fix a field L and a finite etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] morphism y_eta:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(eta), where finite means affine locally finite as a module. Write G=X_eta\times_{\kappa(eta)}\operatorname{Spec}L [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix a finite type I and closed subsets A_i of G covering G. Suppose for every i, every field E and every z:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}L, the inverse image of A_i under G\times_L E\to G is irreducible and nonempty [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there is an open W of S containing eta such that, for every s in W and every field-valued point y:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s), there exist a scheme Z, a surjective morphism p:Z\to X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}K, and irreducible nonempty subsets B_i covering Z, for which A_i\cap A_j nonempty implies B_i\cap B_j nonempty for all i,j. The supplied L, y_eta, I and A_i are preserved; none of these generic data is constructed by this statement.

proof.text: Apply the geometric generic cover model theorem, obtaining an etale model g:T to S, its generic point eta, a finite closed cover C of the pullback, and geometric irreducibility of every field-fibre trace. Record the generic incidence implication from the supplied A to C.

For each pair of indices whose supplied intersection is nonempty, apply the closed-subset fibre nonempty theorem to C_i intersect C_j. For other pairs use the whole base T. Intersect the finitely many resulting open neighbourhoods of eta. Its image under the open etale map g is an open W containing the original generic point.

For s in W choose t in the common open above s. Apply the common-field fibre comparison to the prescribed field K and y. This supplies a field E, a geometric fibre Z over t, and a surjective p to the prescribed test fibre. Define B_i as the inverse image of C_i under the composite of the field-base-change projection and the fibre inclusion. Geometric irreducibility comes from the model theorem and the cover follows by preimage of the union. For an edge, choose a point of C_i intersect C_j over t; use range_fiberι to lift it to the scheme fibre, and surjectivity of field extension to lift it to Z. It lies in both B_i and B_j. Empty I requires no separate case in this assembly: the finite intersection over no pairs is the whole model and the empty cover pulls back to an empty cover.

theorem exists_open_spreading_geometric_generic_cover {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IrreducibleSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    {L : Type u} [Field L]
    (yη : Spec (CommRingCat.of L) ⟶
      Spec (CommRingCat.of (S.residueField (genericPoint S))))
    [IsFinite yη] [Etale yη] {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    (A : I → Set ↥(pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (genericPoint S)) yη))
    (hclosed : ∀ i, IsClosed (A i)) (hcover : (⋃ i, A i) = Set.univ)
    (hgeom : ∀ i, ∀ (E : Type u) (_ : Field E)
      (z : Spec (CommRingCat.of E) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)),
      IsIrreducible ((pullback.fst
        (pullback.snd (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (genericPoint S)) yη) z) ⁻¹' A i)) :
    ∃ (W : Set S), IsOpen W ∧ genericPoint S ∈ W ∧
      ∀ s ∈ W, ∀ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K)
        (y : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of (S.residueField s))),
        ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (p : Z ⟶ pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) y)
          (B : I → Set Z), Surjective p ∧
          (∀ i, IsIrreducible (B i)) ∧ (⋃ i, B i) = Set.univ ∧
          ∀ i j, (A i ∩ A j).Nonempty → (B i ∩ B j).Nonempty
